findings.reason: the plan must name a non-colliding verb or state that the existing `repair-review` is extended, or §4's "the exact `repair-review` command per row" is ambiguous and the implementing node deviates from an exact spec.
findings.text: §3 names its new verb `reckon crew repair-review`, but that command already exists at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:760` (added at `128b1c4dc`, before §3 was authored) with a different signature (`--run --record --set --reason`) and a different purpose (repair a review's status or missing subject identity), and it is the command `reckon/crew/obligations.py:202` emits as a `next_command`; a second `@crew.command(name="repair-review")` on the same group silently overwrites the first in click, so a node implementing §3 exactly either shadows the existing verb and breaks a live caller or must deviate from an exact spec

findings.reason: §3 asserts its refusal is "the complement of §2's rule" and §4 instructs a coordinator to run the verb per listed row, so a listed row the verb refuses makes §4's stated action impossible and falsifies §3's complement claim and the same_revision reasoning on line 84; the fix is to give the verb §2's node-id fallback or to exclude those rows in §2/§4.
findings.text: §3's verb reads the dispatched head only from the row's declared `.at-` write path and refuses "a row with no dispatched head", but §2 (line 60) defines the dispatched head as taken from a declared `.at-` path *or* the hex suffix of the node id, and §2's own known-correct row (line 66) is classified through the node-id suffix; a row whose only dispatched-head source is its node id (no `.at-` path) and whose recorded head does not begin with it is therefore listed by §2 as mismatched yet refused by §3

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every §3 anchor resolves: `_review_record_subject` at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:133`, `carried_revision_pair` in `reckon/crew/review.py` (at :348), `same_revision` at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:102`, the four reader lines `reckon/capabilities.py:968`, `reckon/ledger.py:3702`, `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:377`, `reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:477`, the `repair-status`/`repair-completion` verbs, and the four cited test files all exist; no extensionless href is asserted against.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §3's five done-when items are measurable and the section carries a base-revision negative control (lines 80, 86) that names the reader cases as FAILED by id; a corrected row read with its stale review reddens the base arm on the real reader path.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3's gate and negative-control logs go "under the run directory", a durable crew path, not a session scratchpad or node-local `/tmp`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §3 carries no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers into symbols; `repair-review`, `review_correction` and `_review_record_subject` name mechanisms.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3's verb names a command that already exists, and its dispatched-head source is narrower than §2's, so the two §3 mechanisms below do not hold under the plan's own definitions.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 ships one deliverable, the append-only review-row correction (its accessor and its verb are one mechanism), reviewable on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3 declares `depends-on` on `a-review-promotes-only-its-*#s2` (meta `plan-section-depends-on`), §4 declares `depends-on` on §3, and both landed predecessors (§1 at `c3e988abd`, §2 at `65d442151`) resolve; no relationship points at a wrong node.
